title: Launching an older project version in a newer engine version doesn't seem to upgrade the project
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced on:
- 4.5.1-stable
- 4.6-dev1
- 4.6-dev2

Specifically, upgrading from 4.4 to 4.5 or 4.6, as well as from 4.5 to 4.6.

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable unknown - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu, 23 Oct 2025 18:49:03 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (nvidia; 580.95.05) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9700K CPU @ 3.60GHz (8 threads) - 15.53 GiB memory

### Issue description

Launching a project made with Godot 4.4 in Godot 4.5.1 (or 4.5.1 in 4.6, just tested), the editor rightfully warns that the project will be upgraded. The editor then launches, and the project works with no visible differences. Launching the editor a second time, the project is still listed as being on version the old version, and the editor once again asks to upgrade. Checking the `project.godot` file, the version is indeed still 4.4.

Either the project has silently failed to be upgraded (worst case), or the project file hasn't been updated, I wouldn't know how to check the difference.

_**Additional note**: I have also had some issues launching the editor at all (seems random whether it will launch or not), but it produces no errors in the terminal in these cases, just hangs forever. Might be related, might not, separate issue that's hard to reproduce reliably._

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create new project on older version of editor
2. Launch newer version of editor, edit the project
3. Confirm warning to modify project
4. Close editor, launch it again. Version hasn't changed in the project list

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
